All the facts reproduce. The severity is overstated: nothing is broken and the demo works. This is a missing-enhancement bundle, and two of its claims are weaker than stated. I could not query the live API or DB (locked, and .env is off limits), so I ran Engine.run_population() on a scratch copy of a generated seed-42, 100k-customer DB at scratchpad/algviz/copy.duckdb.

Reproduced:
- **Meter:** It is an 8 px bar with two 2 px ticks (styles.css:117-120). The only threshold explanation is a hover `title` in English with raw decimals, `ask ≥ 0.6 · act ≥ 0.85` (Mirror.tsx:148). The visible text is just "82% sure" (Mirror.tsx:153).
- **Unused weights:** `Evidence.weight` is typed (types.ts:10) but never read in any view. Grep for `weight` in web/src finds only types.ts.
- **Noisy-OR math:** The engine output matches the finding exactly.
  - Sofie's buying_home: weights [0.6, 0.5, 0.1], noisy-OR 0.82, ask threshold 0.6, act threshold 0.85, state ask.
  - Sofie's growing_family: weights [0.35, 0.3] gives 0.545 (moments/growing_family.yaml).
  - The SQL is `1 - exp(sum(ln(1 - weight)))` at dsl.py:200.
- **Log funnel:** Stats were events 6,116,388, signal_hits 23,735, beliefs 21,334, moments 2,468 and messages 2,467. The log bars (ProductOwner.tsx:78,114) come out at 100/64/64/50/50%. On a linear scale they would be 100 / 0.388 / 0.349 / 0.04 / 0.04%. That is about 2,479x fewer messages than events. The last two bars are identical because "moments" = count(state<>'wait') and messages = act+ask+advisor.
- **Silent PO run:** The only feedback during the run is the button text "Running…" (ProductOwner.tsx:91-93). I measured `run_population` at 2.2 to 4.3 s on this machine (run_ms 4002, 2496, 2216, 4291), so the 2.7 s claim is credible.
  - This contradicts the README's "under a second" line for the 0:20 demo beat (README.md:101 and 119).
  - `.funnel-bar div` has `transition: width` (styles.css:176), but a rerun yields the same widths, so nothing moves.
- **No choreography:** styles.css has no `@keyframes`, no `prefers-reduced-motion` and no count-up. GuidanceCard keeps the same key when ask becomes act (Mirror.tsx:115-117). Its content and its `g-ask`→`g-act` border colour swap instantly, with no transition on `.guidance`.
- **Page dimming:** `mutate()` sets `busy` around the whole POST plus reload (Mirror.tsx:31-41), and `.mirror.is-busy` dims the page to 0.75 (styles.css:103). The `transition` exists only on the dimmed state, so it fades in over 0.2 s and snaps back instantly. `refresh_customer` took 46 to 196 ms here, so a short flash on every click is plausible.
- **Duplicate question:** For an `ask` state the BeliefCard shows "That's right / Not true" (Mirror.tsx:187-192) and the GuidanceCard shows "Yes / No" (Mirror.tsx:253-258). Both call the same `feedback()`.
- **Duplicate label:** `users.display_name` for `po` is literally "Product owner" (DB query). App.tsx:45-46 renders it next to ROLE_LABEL "Product owner", so the top bar says it twice.

Why medium rather than high:
- "Barely visible" is overstated. The card already shows a plain-language evidence list: source chip, label, count and last-seen date (Mirror.tsx:157-175), ordered by weight. What is missing is the combination mechanism and a labelled threshold legend.
- The duplicate Yes/No is arguably deliberate. The README demo script uses both surfaces: "She says yes" on the guidance card, then "clicks Not true" on the belief card (README.md:102-103).
- "Largest lever on the score" cannot be verified. The repo contains no judging rubric.
- Most of the suggested fix list (SVG ring, View Transitions, canvas scan grid, cascade) is optional polish. It carries regression risk on demo day.

Given your stated goal of a wow effect on how the algorithm is shown, this is still the highest-value enhancement area. Schedule it by value, not as a defect. The cheap, low-risk wins are:
- a labelled, localized threshold legend;
- segments sized by `weight`;
- a spinner or progress state during the PO run;
- a linear-ratio headline ("about 2,500x fewer to write");
- replacing the `is-busy` dimming;
- fixing the duplicate "Product owner" label.

findings.title: Visual design reads as a generic SaaS admin template; concrete changes for a winning first impression and role/user-adaptive theming
findings.detail: Generic tells: (1) tokens are the default startup palette (Inter-stack, #0b5fff blue on slate on white, 14 px radius, soft shadow; lines 1-25). Inter is named but never loaded (no @font-face or link), so the face is whatever the OS has (Segoe UI on this Windows box); (2) every surface is the same white bordered card with identical rhythm (line 82); (3) a KPI-tile row plus funnel bars plus data table is the stock dashboard; (4) icons are improvised unicode glyphs (⌂ ✿ ◆ ➜ ϟ, Mirror.tsx:6-8); (5) the brand mark is a gradient rounded square (lines 55-59) and the 'Mirror' metaphor appears nowhere visually; (6) motion is limited to 0.15-0.5 s transitions; (7) one theme for every user, apart from the view switch; no dark mode. Positives to keep: the copy is clear and human, NL/FR content is well localised, layout is clean, a two-column Mirror with a 'For you' action column fits above the fold at 1280x720.
findings.evidence: Screenshots of Login, Mirror (EN/NL, phone 375) and PO (1440x900); CSS review of styles.css lines 1-195; font stack computed 'Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, ...'.
findings.fix: Files and changes. (a) App.tsx + styles.css: set `data-role` on the app root and theme per role via CSS variables (customer: warm, large type, friendly; advisor: calm, dense, data-first; PO: dark 'control room'), plus `data-category` on each belief so the accent follows the life moment (housing / family / work), plus prefers-color-scheme. (b) main.tsx: self-host a distinctive variable font via npm (@fontsource-variable/...); the CSP (api.py:82-85) blocks Google Fonts and CDN scripts. (c) Mirror.tsx: a literal 'mirror' hero, left 'what the bank believes', right 'what you see', with a split reflection effect; replace glyph icons with inline SVG set. (d) New views/Live.tsx + App.tsx + api.ts: a split-screen presenter mode, Sofie's phone frame next to the advisor desk and PO counters, polling every 1-2 s (or SSE), using an in-memory token map so one password entry powers all three personas; this shows 'changes everywhere' in one glance and removes the 4 re-logins. (e) Use Intl.NumberFormat / DateTimeFormat / RelativeTimeFormat(lang) so numbers and 'last seen' follow the user's language. (f) Web Speech fallback and an audio waveform for Listen. (g) Login.tsx: a presenter-friendly landing, no dev placeholder. (h) Projector scaling: `html{font-size:clamp(16px,1.05vw,22px)}`, content max-width about 1600. Use only what the CSP allows: CSS, SVG, Canvas 2D, Web Audio, View Transitions and self-hosted assets.
findings.demo_impact: First impression: judges see a competent template rather than a product with a point of view; a role-aware, animated, bilingual experience would differentiate it.

reasons:
The core claims hold, but the severity is too high and three parts of the proposed fix are wrong. I read the code and did not render any view; the authenticated screenshots (including the 1280x720 "fits above the fold" positive) are unverified because the password lives in .env and Vite was not running.

**Confirmed in code**
- Tokens: styles.css:1-25 has #0b5fff, a 14px radius, a soft shadow and `font-family: Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui...`.
- Inter is never loaded. There is no `@font-face`, no link in web/index.html, and package.json has only react, react-dom and dev tooling. Grep of web/src for `@font-face` finds nothing.
- The white-card look is real: `.card` (styles.css:82) is used for belief, guidance, data, funnel and moments panels. The claim that all surfaces are identical is mildly overstated, because `.guidance` adds a coloured left border (lines 146-149) and `.belief.rejected` differs.
- PO is a KPI row, funnel bars and a table (ProductOwner.tsx:97-201).
- Icons are unicode glyphs: Mirror.tsx:6-8 (⌂ ⚭ ✿ ◆ ➜ ϟ ◎), plus ✓ ✕ ▶.
- The brand mark is a gradient rounded square (styles.css:55-59).
- No visual "mirror" concept exists. Grep for `reflect` finds nothing, and the only `mirror` hits are the `.mirror`/`.mirror-grid` class names.
- Motion is only six `transition` rules, 0.05 to 0.5 s (styles.css:68, 103, 118, 140, 141, 176). There is no `@keyframes` and no `startViewTransition`.
- There is one theme: no `prefers-color-scheme`, `data-role` or `data-theme` anywhere in web/src. App.tsx:38 is a plain `<div className="app">`, and only the language adapts per customer.
- The CSP blocks Google Fonts and CDN scripts. api.py:82-85 sets `default-src 'self'; ... style-src 'self'`, and the live server on :8000 returns that exact header. The middleware also covers the SPA, which is served by StaticFiles (api.py:450). Self-hosted fonts are therefore the right route. The Vite dev server on :5173 sets no CSP, so this only bites in the Docker/Cloud Run build.
- The re-login friction is real. The token is memory-only (api.ts:1-2, README:144) and the password field starts empty on each Login mount (Login.tsx:15). The demo script switches persona four times (po, sofie, an, po), so the password is typed four times.
- Login.tsx:52 shows the dev placeholder "DEMO_PASSWORD from your .env". Mirror.tsx:227 and 270 would show "Voice channel not configured (set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY)" (from api.py:313-314) to the audience if no key is set.
- There is no Web Speech fallback; grep for `speechSynthesis` in web/src finds nothing.

**Wrong or overstated parts of the fix**
- (e) is partly already done. `formatDate` already uses per-language locales (i18n.ts:78-81: en-GB, nl-BE, fr-BE), and PO already uses `Intl.NumberFormat("en-BE")` (ProductOwner.tsx:6). The only gap is the `{pct}%` string in i18n.ts:22.
- (h) would do nothing as written. styles.css has no `rem` or `vw` units and every font size is in px, so `html{font-size:clamp(...)}` would change nothing without a px-to-rem conversion.
- (d) polling every 1-2 s would hit the rate limiter. `GET /api/me/guidance` is limited to 30 requests per 60 s per user (api.py:296-298, security.py:99 `"ai": (30, 60)`). Mirror.tsx:18 also calls it on every mutation. Polling at 1 s would return 429s within seconds, and 2 s has no headroom. A live split-screen would need a new cheap endpoint or a higher limit.

**Severity**
Nothing is broken and the demo runs. This is a polish and differentiation gap against the user's "wow" and "adapts to the user" goals, not a functional defect, so medium fits better than high.

The observations hold, but this is a subjective design critique plus a feature wishlist, not a defect, so "high" is too strong. Nothing is broken; I rate it medium. I read the code and loaded the running app at http://localhost:5173 without logging in.

Confirmed in code or in the browser:
- **Tokens** (web/src/styles.css:1-25): #0b5fff accent, #f4f6fa background, white cards, --radius 14px, soft shadow. Font stack is "Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, ...".
- **Inter is never loaded**: there is no @font-face or font link, and web/index.html has no link tags. In the browser, document.fonts lists zero faces, so the text renders in the OS font. web/package.json has no fontsource dependency.
- **One card style everywhere**: .card at styles.css:82 is reused by the belief, guidance and KPI-style panels. The only variation is a coloured left border on .guidance (lines 146-149).
- **Glyph icons**: Mirror.tsx:6-8 uses ⌂ ⚭ ✿ ◆ ➜ ϟ ◎ as category icons. The brand mark is a gradient square (styles.css:55-60).
- **No mirror motif**: Mirror.tsx:69-85 is a plain two-column grid with an h2 "What the bank believes". Nothing visual evokes a mirror.
- **Almost no motion**: the only animated properties are the `transition` rules at styles.css:68, 103, 118, 140-141 and 176, at 0.05 to 0.5 s. There are no @keyframes or `animation` rules, and document.getAnimations() returned 0.
- **No theming**: there is no `data-role`, `data-theme` or `data-category` anywhere in web/src (App.tsx:40-56 renders one static shell), and no `prefers-color-scheme` rule. The browser pane reports prefers-color-scheme: dark and the app still renders light.
- **Login placeholder**: Login.tsx:39 shows the placeholder "DEMO_PASSWORD from your .env" to anyone watching the screen.
- **Re-logins**: README.md:99-106 has the demo going po, sofie, an, po, so four logins. api.ts:1-2 keeps the token in memory only, and a reload logs you out.

Where the finding is wrong or overstated:
1. **Dates already follow language.** Item (e) is mostly moot. i18n.ts:78-80 maps en, nl and fr to en-GB, nl-BE and fr-BE and calls toLocaleDateString. The only fixed locale is ProductOwner.tsx:6 (`Intl.NumberFormat("en-BE")`), and the PO view is English-only.
2. **The CSP point is partly moot.** The CSP (api.py:82-85, `default-src 'self'`, `style-src 'self'`) would block Google Fonts. But it is only sent on FastAPI responses. The README demo path serves the page from Vite on 5173, and its response headers carry no CSP. web/dist does not exist, so api.py:449-450 never mounts the static site, and GET http://localhost:8000/ returns 404. It would bind only on the Cloud Run build. Self-hosting the font is still the right call, because it also removes any dependency on venue Wi-Fi.
3. **Item (f) is partly blocked.** The Permissions-Policy header (api.py:78) sets `microphone=()`, so Web Speech recognition cannot work. speechSynthesis and a Web Audio waveform on the existing blob audio (Mirror.tsx:216-224, allowed by `media-src blob:`) are fine.
4. **Item (d) is risky for today.** The split-screen "Live" view with a token map is a new view plus polling plus a token store. That cuts against the in-memory-only token design noted at api.ts:1-2, and it is a large change for a demo that runs today. The cheap, low-risk items are the self-hosted font, per-role CSS variables including a dark PO control room, `@keyframes` for the meter and funnel, SVG icons and the login placeholder text.
5. **The demo-impact claim is opinion.** "Judges see a template" has no evidence behind it, because the judging criteria are not in the repo.

Nothing in this finding causes a crash, wrong data or a security issue.
